Macy's to close 2 California stores as part of strategic overhaul
FILE - Cars are parked in front of a Macy's store at Hawthorn Mall in Vernon Hills, Ill., June 3, 2024. (AP Photo/Nam Y.
FRESNO, Calif. (FOX26) — Macy's Inc. confirmed that two California stores are among the 14 stores set to close in the coming months.
The West Valley Mall location in Tracy and another in La Mesa will begin clearance sales, expected to begin in mid-January.
The closure of non-go-forward store locations is part of Macy's Bold New Chapter strategy, which aims to return the company to sustainable, profitable sales growth.
This plan, unveiled in Feb. 2024, involves closing approximately 150 underproductive stores over three years while investing in 350 go-forward locations through fiscal 2026.

"Closing any store is never easy, but as part of our Bold New Chapter strategy, we are closing underproductive Macy’s stores to allow us to focus our resources and prioritize investments in our go–forward stores, where customers are already responding positively to better product offerings and elevated service," said Tony Spring, chairman and CEO of Macy’s, Inc.

Since the strategy's inception, investments in pilot Macy’s stores have boosted sales for three consecutive quarters and contributed to record customer satisfaction scores.
Macy's is poised to continue this momentum, focusing on enhancing customer experiences both in-store and online.
Customers can access detailed information about local go-forward stores through the Customer FAQ and Store Locator tool on macys.com.
